patch_description: The current hill-climb spends most of its 1.2s budget on the LP re-solve, but the LP is built with a Python double loop over all 325 pairs plus dense constraint matrices — very slow per iteration, so few moves are evaluated. Two targeted improvements: (1) build the LP constraint matrix vectorized via numpy (triu_indices for pairs) and pass it as a scipy sparse CSR matrix, cutting LP setup cost by ~20-50x; (2) add a cheap vectorized "water-fill" pre-screen (fast_radii) so only moves that improve the fast proxy pay the LP cost, roughly tripling the number of evaluated moves in the same time budget. Both directly implement the recommendation of slack-directed targeted moves being more likely accepted and address wasted evaluations.
